elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant runs "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" — affiliates are covered by the existing (unedited) grant, on the same location-limited scope as Sparkling itself.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither the original nor the rendered grant mentions contractors or personnel acting on Sparkling's behalf; §3(c) still bars sublicensing to "any Person" except a successor or with Garman's written authorization. To reach preferred, insert "and contractors acting on its behalf" into the grant.

The rendered grant states no term; the rationale points to §17(a) ("perpetual while fees are paid") but that provision is not among the cited or rendered paragraphs, so perpetuity for a paid-up licence cannot be verified in operative language.

The rendered grant contains no "irrevocable" wording; equally it contains no at-will revocation right (deterministic check "no at-will revocation remains" ok). Absent the term provisions, express irrevocability cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The licence is fee-based with a Fee Schedule but the termination provisions are not in the cited/rendered text, so whether termination is limited to uncured material breach cannot be assessed.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The added carve-outs are limited to "a successor in a merger or acquisition" in §3(c) and §20(d); transfers to successors by reorganisation or asset transfer outside an M&A remain caught by the consent requirement, so the broader preferred formulation is not achieved.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: The written-notice condition does not apply because the grant already covers affiliates unconditionally: "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations". Coverage without a notice gate is at least as favourable as the fallback, and no edit (and so no duplication) was made.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "non-transferable" is deleted from the grant; §3(c) now reads "except to a successor in a merger or acquisition or as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing"; §20(d) adds "except that Sparkling may assign to a successor in a merger or acquisition." All three blocking provisions are cleared consistently, with no retained sentence contradicting the new permission.

reasons: Fallback is complete: affiliate coverage pre-exists in the grant and all three provisions that barred an M&A successor transfer (the "non-transferable" modifier, §3(c) transfer/sublicence prohibition, §20(d) mutual assignment consent) now carry a Sparkling-only successor path. Position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred is not reached: contractors acting on Customer's behalf are still absent from the grant, and perpetuity/irrevocability/subscription-termination cannot be verified from the rendered text. If preferred is pursued, add "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant and express perpetual/irrevocable wording for paid-up licences.

Minimality holds: each of the three edits is necessary to a single complete fallback level. Deleting "non-transferable" alone would leave §3(c) and §20(d) prohibiting the transfer, and clearing only §3(c) would leave §20(d)'s consent requirement applying to "any rights ... under this Agreement" (i.e. the licence). No affiliate edit was made, so there is no duplicate affiliate coverage; no survival tail, notwithstanding override, or other extras were added; the mutual consent requirement and the Authorized Locations/additional-fee mechanics are retained verbatim.

Intent preserved: the new exceptions run only in Sparkling's (Customer's) favour — no new assignment exception is granted to Garman — and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created. "Successor in a merger or acquisition" is self-describing and not dependent on an undefined trigger.

Drafting note (not a failure): the §3(c) carve-out is placed inside a clause that also governs lease/export/sublicence of the Work; consider confirming the exception is read as attaching to assignment/transfer to a successor rather than to export or sublicensing generally.
